latest_publication.article_format: Ecommerce and wholesale workflow guide with six-state fulfilment exception model
latest_publication.title: How to automate order fulfilment without shipping the wrong orders
latest_publication.target_client_type: UK ecommerce and wholesale teams that repeatedly move orders into warehouse, shipping or fulfilment systems
latest_publication.industry_or_operating_context: Order fulfilment, dispatch readiness, stock checks, address validation, customer changes and exception routing
latest_publication.primary_buyer_problem: Routine orders can move quickly, but stock conflicts, address issues, payment holds and customer changes create fulfilment mistakes when every order is treated the same.
latest_publication.primary_search_intent: Understand how to automate order fulfilment hand-offs while keeping risky exceptions out of dispatch until reviewed.
latest_publication.trend_or_durable_demand: Durable ecommerce and wholesale operational demand. The topic addresses recurring fulfilment, stock and customer-change controls rather than a short-lived trend.
latest_publication.evidence_source_and_date: Repository gap and current Oliver's Consulting article library checked 26 August 2026; no external factual claim required for the core workflow guidance.
latest_publication.existing_article_gap: The site covers stock sync, product data, wholesale order re-keying, purchase orders and returns, but not the downstream fulfilment-readiness decision or exception routing before dispatch.

comparison_against_previous_12.why_meaningfully_distinct: The article focuses on deciding whether an order is safe to enter fulfilment and routing pre-dispatch exceptions. Existing ecommerce articles address upstream inventory, catalogue data, order entry or post-sale returns rather than this operational hand-off.

latest_publication.original_editorial_asset: A six-state fulfilment model covering received, ready, stock exception, address exception, customer change and dispatched.
latest_publication.first_hand_contribution_or_limits: Uses practical ecommerce operations, data and automation framing. It does not prescribe carrier-specific, fraud, tax or payment-provider rules.
latest_publication.proof_points_used_recently: No client outcome or historical proof point is claimed.
